formal.consequent: unused_prd_msbs[i] == aes_prd_get_msbs(prd_masking[i * WidthPRDRow +: WidthPRDRow])  // for all i in [0:3]

assumptions.claim: prd_masking has total bit width at least 4 * WidthPRDRow to support the four indexed part-selects.
assumptions.risk: Bit-select out of range leads to synthesis/simulation errors or silent truncation.

assumptions.claim: Function aes_prd_get_msbs returns a value whose bit width equals the width of each unused_prd_msbs element (likely 1 bit); otherwise truncation or width expansion occurs.
assumptions.risk: Mismatched widths could cause unintended truncation of MSB information or pad with zeroes, potentially affecting observability.

uncertain_points.risk: Observability of mask bits compromises masking-based side-channel countermeasures.

security_implications: The block extracts MSBs from prd_masking (pseudo-random masking material) and drives them to unused_prd_msbs. If unused_prd_msbs is routed to an observable external pin, debug bus, or readable CSR, an attacker could observe mask bits, weakening the DPA/EM side-channel resistance of the AES core. The 'unused' name suggests these signals may be intentionally left floating or tied off; verification must confirm they are not externally accessible. Even if they go to an unconnected output port, synthesis could optimize them away unless preserved, but any exposure is a high-risk security flaw.
